描述_ZN: The eight-volume "Jomei Xuan Ron" is a study of the "Korema Sutra" written by Jia Xiang (549-623), a great master of the Sanlun school of Buddhism during the Sui Dynasty in China. This manuscript is the oldest Buddhist scripture in Japan with a copying date of December 706, and is well known as one of the rarest and most valuable manuscripts in the history of classical sutra copying. Of the eight scrolls, the first scroll was copied in the Heian period (794-1185), the second and fifth scrolls in the Kamakura period (1185-1333), and the other three scrolls, with the exception of the seventh and eighth scrolls, were copied at the beginning. The calligraphic style of the scrolls, which has the flavor of the Six Dynasties, is a valuable document in the history of calligraphy, and the kunten marks attached to each scroll are also noteworthy from the viewpoint of Japanese linguistics.
